text: Given your history of incarceration and the combination of chronic cough, significant weight loss, night sweats, and fever, I need to rule out tuberculosis. REQUEST TEST: Sputum_AFB_stain_and_culture. Do you have anyone else in your household who has a similar cough or illness?

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that "No significant finding" and "Acute appendicitis" are inconsistent with your six-month history of fever, night sweats, and significant weight loss; these are classic signs of tuberculosis, not appendicitis. Given your history of incarceration and current symptoms, the priority is to rule out active pulmonary tuberculosis immediately. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculosis. Given your history of incarceration, chronic cough, night sweats, significant weight loss, and a normal chest X-ray, I suspect pulmonary tuberculosis with possible cavitation not yet visible or an extrapulmonary presentation. We will proceed with starting empiric anti-tubercular therapy pending culture results.
